newsitem.title: USA: Pilots' spokesman says strike "more likely than not".
newsitem.headline: Pilots' spokesman says strike "more likely than not".

text.p: A pilots' union spokesman said Wednesday "there has been no progress so far" in talks on a new contract with American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp., with only days left before a strike deadline.

The spokesman for the Allied Pilots Association, Wally Pitts, told reporters at the end of a bargaining session that the union's view remains that "a strike is more likely than not." The two sides are trying to avert a strike set for midnight Friday against the nation's second biggest airline.
American Airlines made a new pay offer, 6 percent wage increases over four years, up from 5 percent, but the pilots, who have asked for an 11.5 percent increase, rejected the new proposal.
"We're hopeful American Airlines will move toward an agreement rather than away from an agreement as it did last night," Pitts said, referring to the new offer made late on Tuesday.
He said that the union would like to be optimistic, but "there's been no progress so far."

Meanwhile, President Clinton urged the sides to use the current mediation process to resolve their dispute, which he said had huge implications for the country. A strike would disrupt travel plans for hundreds of thousands of people who take American's 2,200 flights worldwide each day.
